read.title: Isogeometric analysis of the Laplace eigenvalue problem on circular sectors: Regularity properties, graded meshes & variational crimes
A Unified CutFEM Formulation for Finite-Strain Elasticity: Energy Minimisation and Corner Singularities

results.statement: Main transfer result (Section 6 / linear part of Theorem 3, referenced): the CutFEM solution on a locally refined background mesh has the same energy-norm rate R(h) as the matching (body-fitted) mesh with the same local refinement. The constants do not depend on how the boundary cuts the mesh. The linear case follows from quasi-optimality in the local-size norm |||·|||_g plus Assumption 3.
results.norm: local-size mesh-dependent energy norm |||·|||_g (bulk gradient + Nitsche boundary term sum_T ||h_T^{-1/2} v||^2_{∂Ω∩T} + ghost-penalty seminorm with local face size h_F)
results.rate_formula: |||u - u_h|||_g <= C R(h), where R(h) is the matching-mesh interpolation rate in (57). The passage does not give R(h) explicitly; it is imported from [67,68]. Radial grading (56): h_T ≃ h^{1/µ} on the core patch, h_T ≃ h r_T^{1-µ} elsewhere. #T_h = O(h^{-2}) for every µ, so the rate in h equals the rate per DOF: beta = (rate in h)/2. Classical value (imported, not stated in the passage): R(h) = h^{min(p, λ/µ)} (with a log factor at equality). Nodes s^g correspond to µ = 1/g, so beta = min(p, λ g)/2.
results.assumptions: Domain: unfitted (CutFEM) domain with a corner/junction x0 where the solution has the singular mode r^λ Φ. Background family {T_h} with radial grading parameter µ ∈ (0,1] toward x0, uniform shape regularity, bounded neighbour-size ratio and bounded active-layer width. Assumption 2: local-size cut trace inequality, ghost-penalty extension, Nitsche coercivity (penalty γ/h_T) and local interpolation estimates hold with constants independent of the cut and of the refinement level (proof deferred to Appendix A, Prop. 3). Assumption 3: a stable extension Eu ∈ H^1(Ω_T)^d exists and the conforming interpolant satisfies (57). Polynomial degree p is not fixed in the passage. Nonlinear (finite-strain) version is conditional: it also needs the local-size differentiability and Jacobian-defect hypotheses of Theorem 3, which are not in the passage.
results.regularity: u = regular part + r^λ Φ, with |D^k (r^λ Φ)| ~ r^{λ-k}. Not in H^{p+1}. Weighted-space regularity on the core patch, elementwise H^{p+1} away from x0. Analytic continuation of the singular mode into the fictitious sector.
results.quote: the rate a matching mesh achieves with a given local refinement, the CutFEM discretisation on the same background refinement inherits, with constants independent of how ∂Ω cuts the mesh

results.statement: L2 counterpart in Assumption 3: the interpolation error satisfies ||e_h||_{L2(Ω_T)} <= C h R(h). The assumed dual approximability (|||Eφ_g - I_h Eφ_g|||_g <= C h ||g||) is the Aubin–Nitsche ingredient for an L2 estimate of the FE error of the same order h R(h).
results.norm: L2(Ω_T) (interpolation error); implied L2(Ω) FE error via duality
results.rate_formula: ||e_h||_{L2} <= C h R(h). For the FE error via duality: ||u - u_h||_{L2} <~ h R(h). With the classical R(h) = h^{min(p, λ g)} and #T_h = O(h^{-2}): beta = (1 + min(p, λ g))/2. This only holds when the dual bound with factor h holds, which needs λ g >= 1 (µ <= λ).
results.assumptions: Everything in Assumptions 2 and 3, plus: for every g ∈ L2(Ω)^d, the linearised adjoint solution φ_g has a stable extension with |||Eφ_g - I_h Eφ_g|||_g <= C h ||g||_{L2(Ω)}, with C independent of h. The dual problem has the same corner singularity, so this needs grading strong enough that the dual error is O(h): λ/µ >= 1. With λ = 0.5445 this means g >= 1/λ ≈ 1.84. For g = 1.5 the dual assumption fails (dual rate h^{0.817}), so no beta is given for g = 1.5.
results.regularity: Same as the energy result. The dual solution has the same r^λ singularity.
results.quote: ||| eh |||g ≤ C R(h), ∥eh ∥L2 (ΩT ) ≤ C h R(h)

results.statement: Quasi-uniform special case: when µ = 1, h_T ~ h_F ~ h, |||·|||_g reduces to the global triple norm (26), and Section 3 is the special case of uniform refinement. With a corner singularity, the uniform-mesh energy rate is limited by λ.
results.rate_formula: |||u - u_h||| <= C R(h). On uniform meshes the classical rate (imported, not stated in the passage) is R(h) = h^{min(p, λ)}, so beta = min(p, λ)/2, independent of p once p >= 1 > λ.
results.assumptions: Quasi-uniform background mesh (µ = 1), Section 3 stability (Proposition 1, Corollary 2), extension/approximability as in Assumption 3.
results.quote: On a quasi-uniform mesh hT ∼ hF ∼ h, so ||| · |||g reduces to the global triple norm (26) and Section 3 is the special case of uniform refinement.

results.statement: Classical body-fitted theory, cited: with the correct grading, the optimal rates are known, and adaptive refinement reaches the same rate per degree of freedom without knowing the singular exponent in advance.
results.rate_formula: Optimal rate per DOF, i.e. the smooth-solution rate: energy error ~ N^{-p/2} in 2D. The passage states this qualitatively and does not give a formula.
results.assumptions: Body-fitted discretisation; a priori grading with the correct parameter [67,68,43], or adaptive (a posteriori) refinement. Exponent λ need not be known for adaptivity. Degree p is not specified.
results.regularity: Corner singularity r^λ Φ with known or unknown λ.
results.quote: the singular exponents, the correct grading parameter, and the resulting optimal rates are all known [67, 68, 43], and adaptive refinement attains the same rate per degree of freedom without prior knowledge of the exponent

read.title: A fitted scheme for a Caputo initial-boundary value problem

results.statement: Standard L1 scheme for a time-fractional (Caputo, order α) reaction-diffusion problem on a graded temporal mesh (cited as [18, Theorem 5.3]): the maximum nodal error is bounded by C(h^2 + N^{-min{2-α, rα}}). Consequences stated: r = 1 (uniform mesh) gives temporal order α; r ≥ (2-α)/α gives temporal order 2-α. Tables 1-2 are said to agree with this. NOT a finite-element result: it is a finite-difference/L1 time-stepping estimate in the discrete maximum norm, not in the energy norm, L2 norm or a functional.
results.norm: discrete maximum nodal error max_{(x_m,t_n) in Q̄} |u(x_m,t_n) - u_m^n| (discrete L∞; not energy, L2 or a functional)
results.rate_formula: max |u(x_m,t_n) - u_m^n| ≤ C (h^2 + N^{-min{2-α, rα}}); r = 1 gives order α in time, r ≥ (2-α)/α gives order 2-α in time
results.assumptions: Time-fractional problem with a Caputo derivative D_t^α, 0<α<1 (α = 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 tested), on Q = space interval × (0,T]. Spatial mesh is uniform with mesh size h (M intervals) and second-order spatial discretisation. Temporal mesh is graded with grading exponent r: t_n = T(n/N)^r is implied by the later Example 2 definition t_n = (n/(2N))^r; this formula is not stated explicitly for (5.1). The solution has the typical weak singularity at t = 0 (see [18]). The constant C is generic and its dependence on T is not stated for this scheme. The full hypotheses of [18, Thm 5.3] are not reproduced in the passage. No finite-element degree is involved.
results.regularity: Weak initial-layer singularity in time at t = 0 (as for typical solutions of time-fractional problems, e.g. derivatives behaving like t^{α-k}); the exact regularity class is given in [18] and is not stated in the passage.
results.quote: In [18, Theorem 5.3] it is established that the standard L1 scheme on a graded mesh satisfies the error estimate

results.statement: Fitted scheme (3.5) on a uniform temporal mesh (r = 1): Theorem 4 gives a temporal order of convergence of min{2α, 2-α} for the maximum nodal error. Table 3 is said to agree with this. NOT a finite-element energy/L2 result.
results.rate_formula: error = O(N^{-min{2α, 2-α}}) in time for r = 1 (spatial part presumably O(h^2), not stated explicitly here)
results.assumptions: Fitted scheme (3.5) for a Caputo time-fractional problem, 0<α<1. Uniform spatial mesh with M intervals and uniform temporal mesh (r = 1). Weak singularity at t = 0. The full statement and hypotheses of Theorem 4 are not reproduced in the passage. The numerical growth rates indicate that the constant depends on the final time T approximately as O(T^{2α}).
results.regularity: Weak singularity at t = 0; the precise regularity class is not stated in the passage.
results.quote: Note that when r = 1, Theorem 4 indicates that the order is min{2α, 2 − α}

results.statement: Fitted scheme (3.5) on a graded temporal mesh with optimal grading r = max{1, (2-α)/(2α)}: by Remark 5 the temporal order of convergence is 2-α. Tables 4-5 are said to agree with this. The T-dependence of the error is approximately O(T^{2-α}) if α < 2/3 and O(T^{2α}) if α ≥ 2/3 (Remark 5). Remark 6 covers the uniform-mesh T-dependence for α < 2/3. NOT a finite-element energy/L2 result.
results.rate_formula: error = O(N^{-(2-α)}) in time with r = max{1, (2-α)/(2α)}; the constant grows like T^{2-α} (α < 2/3) or T^{2α} (α ≥ 2/3)
results.assumptions: Fitted scheme (3.5) for a Caputo time-fractional problem, 0<α<1. Uniform spatial mesh. Graded temporal mesh t_n ∝ (n/N)^r with r = max{1, (2-α)/(2α)}. Weak singularity at t = 0. The full statements of Theorem 4, Remark 5 and Remark 6 are not reproduced in the passage.
results.regularity: Weak singularity at t = 0; the precise regularity class is not stated in the passage.
results.quote: by Remark 5 the order is 2 − α if the optimal grading is used
